title: Fastbridge SDK orchestration playbook (sketch)
content:
Summary:

This is a working sketch for a small, composable SDK onboarding playbook that focuses on orchestration primitives ("fastbridge") rather than one giant monolithic client. The goal is to provide a 10–15 minute 'first success' path for engineers integrating Redwood APIs while also giving clear extension points for advanced production features (caching, circuit breakers, telemetry).

Context / Problem we see:
- Developers often want a tiny working example that wires a request end-to-end (local dev -> Redwood hosted endpoint -> display) but then hit cross-cutting concerns (retries, batching, auth refresh, observability) when ramping to QA/prod.
- Current SDK samples demonstrate single-call usage but do not show how to compose small pieces (auth adapter + retry + batching + metrics) into a repeatable pattern.
- We want a repeatable mental model that scales from prototype to production without rewriting application logic.

Goals:
- Deliver a minimal "fastbridge" composition pattern: 3 small building blocks (Transport, Policy, Adapter) that are idiomatic in JS and Python.
- A 10-minute quickstart that returns streaming text from the API and shows token-level telemetry.
- Provide checklists for migrating from prototype to prod (pin model, add quantization hints, enable KV cache).
- Include explicit failure-mode guidance and sample SLOs to set expectations.

Design principles (working):
- Small is better: each package has a single responsibility and a clear public surface.
- Composable by default: policies are middleware-style and can be layered in any order.
- Local-first dev: easy simulator for the runtime (lightweight stubs) so people can iterate offline.
- Observable: include a recommended telemetry contract that surfaces request_id, route, model, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_kind.

Fastbridge building blocks (high level):
- Transport (low level): HTTP/gRPC client that knows API base URL, API key, region. Exposes `send(req)` and a streaming `stream(req)` for incremental responses.
- Policy (middleware): retry, backoff, circuit-breaker, batching, timeouts. Policies wrap Transport.
- Adapter (high level): model-specific helpers (completionAdapter, embedAdapter, chatAdapter) that normalize request/response shapes and map fields used by telemetry.

Quickstart outline (developer flow - JS):
1) npm init; install @rw/fastbridge-transport + @rw/fastbridge-policies + @rw/fastbridge-adapters
2) Create a very small main.js:
   - import FastTransport, composePolicies, chatAdapter
   - wire apiKey from env, create transport, compose a RetryPolicy + TimeoutPolicy, wrap transport
   - call chatAdapter.chat({ messages: [..], model: 'rw-small-1' }) and stream tokens to stdout

Minimal pseudo-example (JS):

const transport = new FastTransport({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.ai' });
const policies = composePolicies(new RetryPolicy(), new TimeoutPolicy(5000));
const client = policies.wrap(transport);
const chat = new ChatAdapter(client);
for await (const token of chat.stream({ model: 'rw-small-1', messages })) {
  process.stdout.write(token.text);
}

Local dev: run a dev shim that simulates streaming and rate limits. `fastbridge dev --seed sample-responses.json` should return identical shapes so front-end devs can build UI without an account.

Telemetry contract (proposal):
- Events: request_start, request_end, token_emitted, error
- request_start attrs: request_id, route, model, user_agent, input_tokens_est
- request_end attrs: request_id, model, total_tokens_in, total_tokens_out, latency_ms, success=true/false, error_kind
- token_emitted attrs: request_id, token_index, token_text_length, cumulative_tokens_out
- Transport must emit request_id (UUID v4) on every call and propagate it to the adapter and telemetry sinks.

Migration checklist (prototype -> staging):
- Pin model version (avoid latest tag)
- Add prefix K/V cache for repeated prompts or context-heavy agents
- Replace local dev transport with real transport + use canary routing config for routing policy
- Enable cost/latency sampling and verify telemetry fields are present
- Add E2E tests that replay the quickstart conversation and assert tokens_out > 0 and latency < 2s for sample prompt

Failure modes & mitigation (short):
- Burst throttling: expose 429 surface to apps with `retry-after` header; include an exponential backoff policy and a graceful degrade adapter that returns cached stub responses for non-critical flows.
- Token cutoff/regression: add a lightweight regression test (prompt + expected golden suffix tokens) in CI. If regression detected, auto-create a draft on PR with failing eval attached.
- Partial stream drop: policy should provide a fallback to `non-streaming` API path; UI must accept incremental patches and not assume single final delta.

Acceptance criteria for this playbook: (MVP)
- A newcomer can run `npm i` and `node main.js` to see a streaming response in < 15 minutes.
- The code samples include a working RetryPolicy and a sample telemetry emitter that forwards to console and an OTLP-compatible collector.
- A local dev shim exists and is used by at least two internal demo apps.

Open questions / TBD
- Scope of official language support beyond JS/Python (go/ts-runtimes?). Keep it minimal for MVP.
- Do we ship the 'dev shim' as a separate binary (fastbridge) or as a node package CLI?
- SDK surface: do we expose adapters as classes or pure functions to simplify tree-shaking?

Next steps (concrete short list):
- 11/10: alignment sync with serving-runtime to confirm telemetry fields and streaming contract (owner: Asha)
- 11/17: prototype `fastbridge-transport` + `chatAdapter` and a single-page demo app (owner: Owen)
- 11/24: internal demo & feedback + add local shim (owner: Leila)
- 12/01: decide on package boundaries and publish draft README templates (owner: Asha)

Appendix: quick UX notes for docs writer
- Provide a one-click 'run in cloud' badge that runs the sample with ephemeral key and shows live stream (sandboxed).
- Keep first sample under 50 lines, emphasise that policies are optional (show 3-line version).
- Add a "what to do next" section after quickstart for obvious production steps.

Notes to self: rough heuristics for the team micro-UX experiment: prefer composition over inheritance; avoid heavy DI frameworks; make the shim resilient to noisy CI environments.

-- end sketch --
